title: "Worked example"
description: "An illustrative request showing how model routing becomes a ranking."
---

## Illustrative only

Suppose the fabricated request is: “Explain why my balcony basil leaves are
turning yellow, then give me a safe two-week recovery plan.” The fabricated
candidates are **GardenGuide**, **CodeTutor**, and **QuickFacts**. No private
collected response appears in this example.

GardenGuide might rank first because prior requests and its candidate profile
suggest strength in plant diagnosis and actionable plans. QuickFacts might rank
second because it can answer factual pieces but is less reliable for a staged
plan. CodeTutor ranks last because its evidence concerns software, not plants.

The research question is not whether those names sound plausible. It is which
signals can produce a useful ordering consistently across development requests,
without borrowing the relevance labels for the request being ranked.
